text_blocks.snippet: Balanitis treatment depends on the cause, but often involves topical or oral medications. Common treatments include antibiotics for bacterial infections, antifungal creams for yeast infections, and steroid creams for inflammation. In some cases, circumcision may be recommended, especially for recurrent infections.
snippet_highlighted_words: antibiotics for bacterial infections, antifungal creams for yeast infections, and steroid creams for inflammation

list.title: Antibiotics:
list.snippet: If a bacterial infection is the cause, oral antibiotics like amoxicillin or erythromycin, or topical antibiotic creams like mupirocin, may be prescribed.

list.title: Antifungal Creams:
list.snippet: For yeast infections (like Candida), antifungal creams like clotrimazole, miconazole, or ketoconazole are commonly used. In some cases, oral antifungals like fluconazole may be necessary.

list.title: Steroid Creams:
list.snippet: If inflammation is a significant symptom, a steroid cream like hydrocortisone or a stronger corticosteroid may be used to reduce inflammation.

list.title: Antihistamines:
list.snippet: If an allergic reaction is suspected, antihistamines might be recommended.

list.title: Hygiene:
list.snippet: Keeping the affected area clean and dry is crucial. Gentle washing with warm water and avoiding harsh soaps or lotions can help.

list.title: Diabetes Management:
list.snippet: If balanitis is linked to diabetes, proper diabetes management, including blood sugar control, is essential.

list.title: Circumcision:
list.snippet: In cases of recurrent balanitis, especially with phimosis (tight foreskin), circumcision may be recommended to prevent future infections.
If symptoms don't improve with over-the-counter treatments or hygiene measures.
If the balanitis is severe or recurrent.
If there is an underlying condition like diabetes.
